agricultural: broad cultivated land with regular field texture and open farmland layout, distinguishing agricultural from runway by lacking a long straight paved strip, from golfcourse by weaker landscaped fairway structure, and from harbor by lacking dock-water organization.
airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway which appears as a long straight paved strip without a discrete fuselage.
baseballdiamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield, distinguishing baseballdiamond from buildings by lacking large roof-dominant structures, from parkinglot by lacking organized vehicle-row layout, and from storagetanks by lacking circular industrial tank geometry.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, visually distinct from inland land-cover classes by direct coastal water contact.
buildings: large roofed man-made structures with block-like geometry and organized built-up layout, distinguishing buildings from denseresidential by stronger individual roof mass, from baseballdiamond by lacking sports-field geometry, and from parkinglot by having dominant roof coverage rather than open paved space.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from river by lacking a continuous water channel, from golfcourse by weaker man-made landscaping, and from tenniscourt by lacking small rectangular court markings.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing denseresidential from mediumresidential by much closer building intervals, from buildings by smaller more repetitive residential roofs, and from sparseresidential by a far denser neighborhood texture.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture and little visible built structure, distinguishing forest from golfcourse by lacking designed fairways, from denseresidential by lacking repetitive roof clusters, and from river by lacking a continuous watercourse.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous road surface and linear traffic structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended roadway flow, from runway by lacking aviation-strip context, and from intersection by being a corridor rather than a compact junction node.
golfcourse: well-maintained green fairways with landscaped grass regions and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golfcourse from forest by weaker canopy continuity, from agricultural by less regular cultivated parcel structure, and from chaparral by stronger man-made landscaping.
harbor: waterfront port area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from golfcourse by clear water and dock context, from agricultural by lacking cultivated field texture, and from parkinglot by stronger shoreline-water organization.
intersection: road crossing region where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from freeway by emphasizing a compact junction node, from denseresidential by road-dominant geometry rather than dense housing roofs, and from overpass by weaker elevated crossing structure.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible yards and balanced housing density, distinguishing mediumresidential from denseresidential by larger spacing between houses, from sparseresidential by denser neighborhood grouping, and from buildings by weaker large-roof dominance.
mobilehomepark: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobilehomepark from denseresidential by more uniform trailer-like organization, from parkinglot by lacking vehicle-row layout, and from sparseresidential by denser and more regular placement.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from runway by lacking a long flat aviation strip.
parkinglot: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parkinglot from mobilehomepark by lacking trailer-like housing rows, from buildings by weaker roof dominance, and from baseballdiamond by lacking sports-field geometry.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from chaparral by clear water appearance, from forest by water-dominant linear structure, and from mobilehomepark by lacking repeated housing rows.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open surroundings, distinguishing runway from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body, from freeway by weaker branching road-network structure, and from agricultural by lacking cultivated field texture.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparseresidential from denseresidential by far lower roof density, from buildings by weaker large-structure dominance, and from mobilehomepark by lacking regular trailer-row organization.
storagetanks: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storagetanks from buildings by stronger circular-container dominance, from harbor by weaker dock-water context, and from baseballdiamond by lacking sports-field geometry.
tenniscourt: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated sports-court geometry, distinguishing tenniscourt from denseresidential by lacking residential roof clusters, from chaparral by lacking natural shrub texture, and from sparseresidential by lacking scattered housing structures.
